author: Good Enough
description:
Doctors removed parts of patients’ brains, and called it treatment.

In insane asylums, lobotomies were performed to change behavior and “calm” patients, often by severing connections in the brain. The procedure was widely used despite the severe and permanent effects it had on patients’ personalities and cognitive function.

This video explores one of the most disturbing practices in medical history and what patients were forced to endure.

author: Good Enough
description:
Doctors once drilled holes into people’s skulls, and this was considered treatment.

In early forms of medicine, trepanation was used to relieve pressure or “release spirits,” with some procedures creating openings large enough to expose parts of the brain. Despite the risks, this practice was performed for centuries across different cultures.

This video explores one of the most disturbing medical practices in history and what patients were forced to endure.
